correctness.rationale: The continuous functional calculus reduces the integrand to max of two squared real projections. The 2x2 real matrix vv^T-ww^T has trace a-b, determinant -c^2; the absolute one-harmonic average evaluates exactly to the piecewise arctangent formula, including h=0/c=0. Differentiation gives c²/(h²+c²); Taylor expansion gives the nonzero cubic coefficient for unequal fixed moduli and exact sine law for equal moduli. Actual packaged script passes 12 quadrature cases, 3 phase chains, and 6 asymptotic diagnostics; these tests supplement the proof.

originality.rationale: The focal 2026 full text provides general bounds only. Relevant published full-text results cover unitary equal-radius spectra, zero-eigenvalue rank-one cases, and one perpendicular unequal-radius example with generic cubic stability, but none gives an exact formula for arbitrary unequal radial moduli and arbitrary relative phase, its two-spectral-point lower certificate, or the fixed-radii phase asymptotic. Specific overlapping special cases are explicitly excluded as contributions. Residual risk of equivalent convex-geometric cosine-average identities remains.

value.rationale: This is the complete, sharp quantitative classification of the smallest nontrivial normal spectral family for a newly introduced operator-radius invariant. Its two-point inequality works for arbitrary normal operators, and its radial-degeneracy transition is precise: cubic phase sensitivity at unequal fixed moduli becomes linear exactly when moduli coalesce. Previously established equal-radius unitary, zero-rank, and perpendicular slices cannot determine the interior two-parameter profile; the result is structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary scalar computation.
